summary: iter62 — Mandatory device-capture screenshot during registration. Full backend + frontend e2e validation done. All 11 backend pytest cases pass: /auth/ocr-device-info (3 cases: empty rejected, data-URL accepted, bare-b64 accepted), /auth/register validation (6 cases: missing capture/kind/product/model/device_name/pseudo all return 400; valid phone + valid computer return 200 with verification_link), and full regression e2e (register → verify-email → login → 200). UI confirmed: tab-signup reveals DeviceCaptureField between pseudo (467px) and email (825px) at 576px, dropzone has data-testid='device-capture-dropzone', file input has 'device-capture-input'. Submit without capture displays sonner toast 'Capture de l'appareil requise…' and BLOCKS the /auth/register request (intercepted, not fired). Regression: legacy login for test_dash_1777658375@gmail.com / Pass1234 still returns 200 with session_token.

issues: The Capture d'écran helper paragraph is only in French while the rest of the signup form uses i18n keys (Sign up / Create my account / Your pseudonym are English here). Minor i18n inconsistency — strings inside DeviceCaptureField.jsx are hardcoded French.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:629-746 — RegisterRequest fields and the OCR endpoint are placed right above /auth/register which is good locality. The validations at L772-791 are clear and return explicit French messages — good UX.

DeviceCaptureField.jsx is well-structured (203 lines, single responsibility, exposes 5 data-testids). Paste listener attached to document is global; harmless on /login but consider scoping to the dropzone element if reused on pages where other paste handlers exist.
Frontend validation at Login.js:291-297 mirrors backend rules exactly — good defense in depth. Both server and client reject the same edge cases.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (dropzone visible, validation blocks submit, toast shown, request intercepted)

context_for_next_testing_agent: iter62 is fully green. Frontend integration confirmed via UI: signup → fill pseudo/email/password (no capture) → click 'Create my account' → toast 'Capture de l'appareil requise…' appears + /auth/register NOT called.
